# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 1 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 1:4 — description of Aseneth's superiority: "excelling" vs. "surpassing"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "excelling all the virgins of the earth" | Literal Greek hyperbolē |
| LOGOS | "surpassing all the virgins of the earth" | Standard formal English |
| PNEUMA | "more stunning than any woman in the land" | Idiomatic; compresses scope |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "surpassing." PNEUMA narrows "earth" to "land" losing the universal scope. EMET's "excelling" is acceptable but slightly archaic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:11 — Pharaoh's rebuke: clause structure

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Why do you seek a wife who is beneath you?" | Literal question form |
| LOGOS | "Why do you seek a wife beneath your station?" | Adds "station" for clarity |
| PNEUMA | "Why would you marry someone below your rank?" | Merges two clauses |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Station" makes explicit what the Greek implies. PNEUMA's compression loses the rhetorical force of the two-part rebuke.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:14 — "gods" vs. "idols"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "gods of Egypt" | Greek theoi — literal |
| LOGOS | "idols of Egypt" | Interpretive; reflects narrator's theological stance |
| PNEUMA | "Egyptian idols" | Same interpretive move, reordered |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Split: verse 14 uses "idols" (narrator's evaluative voice) but note that Aseneth herself would call them "gods." LOGOS adopted.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Theologically significant.

---

## 1:15 — chamber count and contents: one room or two?

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Two separate verses for adornments and attendants | Follows longer recension |
| LOGOS | Combined into one verse | Follows shorter recension |
| PNEUMA | Combined, adding "devoted to them" | Paraphrase expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted combined verse (LOGOS) following the shorter recension as more primitive. PNEUMA's addition "devoted" has no Greek basis.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Textual variant.

---
